name: mio_basic
kind: installation, supersedes version 3 (whose K2 failed on the 1.0-cycle classes); frozen before any replay of an engine with the changed rule; no new GPU data. Rules M1, M3, M4, the leaves and the criteria K1-K5 are those of version 3 word for word; only M2 (and the sentence of `turn` that states it) is reworded: the per-SM server grants the earliest free interval instead of advancing one frontier
mechanisms: instruction.service (S2R, LDS, SHFL.BFLY, SHFL.IDX, S2UR, LDC, LDCU, CS2R.CLOCK, VOTE)
MIO queue (mio_throttle; new ledger reason mio_inflight)
why: Version 3 addendum: with one frontier per SM and class the cycles between a warp's own turns (2 apart on its chain) cannot serve other warps, and the saturated LDS / SHFL.BFLY cells take 480 / 950 cycles per iteration where the hardware takes producers x 1.0 = 256 / 510. A server that serves one instance per q cycles whenever a request is waiting uses those cycles.
data_seen_before_freezing: Everything listed in version 3 (data (a)-(f) there stand unchanged and are referred to by the same letters).

The version 3 replay mio_basic-v3r1 (build 0a919d02) and its verdicts (version 3 addendum): K1, K3, K4, K5 pass on both devices; K2 passes for S2R / S2UR / LDC and fails for LDS / SHFL.BFLY at 16 per warp x 16 and x 32 warps (+84 to +92 %).

(g) Hand check of the reworded M2 on the failing shape: warp A's LDS turns at 0, 2, 4, ...; a second warp's requests take 1, 3, 5, ...; with 16 or 32 warps every cycle of the server is used and the period is producers x 1.0 as on hardware. For q = 2.0 with r = 2.0 (S2R, S2UR, LDC) the reworded rule grants the same turns as the frontier whenever requests arrive in a backlog, so the four passing K2 cells are expected unchanged. No engine with the reworded rule has been run.

rules.fields: New fields of the instruction.service leaf (schema instruction_template; absent or 0 = the rule does not apply and timing is bit for bit as before): return_interval_cycles (float64, cycles), return_chain (uint64, enum, 1-7), sm_service_interval_cycles (float64, cycles), warp_inflight_group (uint64, count).
rules.turn: An instance whose leaf has return_interval_cycles r > 0 or sm_service_interval_cycles q > 0 takes a turn when it issues. Issue itself is not delayed by M1 or M2. eligible = max(issue cycle, chain_free of its warp and chain (if r > 0)). turn_start = eligible if q = 0; otherwise the earliest time t >= eligible at which the server of its SM and operation class has no granted interval overlapping [t, t + q) (M2). Then chain_free = turn_start + r and the server is granted [turn_start, turn_start + q). Turns are granted in issue order. Times are kept as fractions; a whole-cycle view takes the ceiling. No turn: a predicated-off instance; an instance whose access is remote shared memory (its timing stays as today).
rules.M1: Per warp and return_chain one chain_free. Every term of the instance's result that counts from its issue cycle today counts from turn_start: the service result latency; for LDS the storage.shared.issue row (result = turn_start + the row's cycles + completion latency; an instance that takes a turn neither reads nor advances the row's per-SMSP frontier, and its read barrier is released at turn_start as it is at the row's start today); for LDC / LDCU the re-read term of constant_paths C2 (line resident and filled: ready at turn_start + reread; fill in flight: max(turn_start + reread, fill ready); line not resident: unchanged, the fill starts at issue). Chains: 1 = S2R, LDS, SHFL.BFLY, SHFL.IDX; 2 = LDC; 3 = S2UR; 4 = LDCU (b300).
rules.M2: Per SM and operation class one server (S2R, S2UR, LDC: q = 2.0; LDS, SHFL.BFLY: q = 1.0). The server holds the set of intervals it has granted; a new turn takes the earliest interval of length q at or after the instance's eligible time that overlaps none of them, so the cycles between one warp's turns serve other warps. Granted intervals that end at or before the current cycle are forgotten. Classes do not queue behind each other.
rules.M3: Per warp and chain a count. Whenever the chain is idle (current cycle >= chain_free) the count is 0. An instance whose leaf has warp_inflight_group g > 0 cannot issue while the count is >= g and the current cycle < chain_free: it waits at issue until chain_free (ledger reason mio_inflight, mapped to mio_throttle), at which cycle the count is 0. Each issue of an instance with g > 0 adds 1. g = 4 for S2UR, LDC and b300 LDCU.
rules.M4: Leaves only: CS2R.CLOCK and VOTE take 2.0 cycles of the unit alu_smsp (VOTE moves there from shfl_smsp; common/class_resource.json follows) and their result latency is 2, so a reader behind the unit turn does not wait on the scoreboard.

leaves.S2R: issue_interval_cycles 0 (h100 was 2; b300 is 0), return_interval_cycles 2.0, return_chain 1, sm_service_interval_cycles 2.0; result latency unchanged (23).
leaves.LDS: return_interval_cycles 2.0, return_chain 1, sm_service_interval_cycles 1.0; result latency and the storage.shared.issue leaf unchanged.
leaves.SHFL.BFLY: issue_interval_cycles 0 (was 3.99 / 3.99), return_interval_cycles 2.0, return_chain 1, sm_service_interval_cycles 1.0; result latency unchanged (24).
leaves.SHFL.IDX: issue_interval_cycles 0 (was 4.0 / 3.99), return_interval_cycles 4.0, return_chain 1; result latency unchanged (26.0).
leaves.S2UR: issue_interval_cycles 0 (h100 was 2), return_interval_cycles 2.0, return_chain 3, sm_service_interval_cycles 2.0, warp_inflight_group 4; result latency unchanged (35).
leaves.LDC: return_interval_cycles 2.0, return_chain 2, sm_service_interval_cycles 2.0, warp_inflight_group 4; memory.constant_cache unchanged.
leaves.LDCU (b300 only): return_interval_cycles 2.0, return_chain 4, warp_inflight_group 4; memory.constant_cache unchanged. The h100 leaf is not changed (sm_90a emits ULDC, a fixed-latency instruction whose reader never waits).
leaves.CS2R.CLOCK: result_latency_cycles = completion_latency_cycles = 2 (h100 was 14, b300 placeholder 1), issue_interval_cycles 2.0 (was 6.0 / 0), resource alu_smsp (unchanged).
leaves.VOTE: result_latency_cycles = completion_latency_cycles = 2 (was 13), issue_interval_cycles 2.0 (was 2.0 / 2.03), resource alu_smsp (was shfl_smsp).
leaves.evidence: measured; new source records mio_basic.h100.v1, mio_basic.h100.v2, mio_basic.b300.v1, mio_basic.b300.v2 (artifacts: the tables named under data_seen). M1 / M4 values and the group of four cite v1 (the group also v2), the per-SM intervals cite v2. return_chain is structural (data (d)); the membership of SHFL.IDX and the separate chain of LDCU are assumptions and say so in the source text.

replay: Every cell of sync_basic v1 / v2 / v4 (53 per device), branch_basic v1 (23 per device; the v cells from branch_basic-v) and mio_basic v1 / v2 (83 per device: mio_basic-r3 56, mio_basic-v2 without its void w32 rows 23, mio_basic-v2w32 4) is replayed from its existing capture with the new formal build (clean clone, seven gates) into $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/mio_basic-v4r1/<device>/<source>/sim; 'before' is build 68702860 (branch_basic-v2r3 for the sync_basic / branch_basic sources if it is the 68702860 replay, else a replay of that build made for this purpose; <source>/<device>/sim for the mio_basic sources). Verdicts by tools/microbench/mio_basic/judge_v3.py, unchanged (the criteria are those of version 3). Quantities as in versions 1 / 2: extended total = sum over the loop-body pcs and the pc behind the last one, per iteration (hardware = scaled samples of every class, mean of the passes with at least 1500 samples; replay = every ledger reason / warps); T = extended total - extended total of m.nop of the same shape + 3 (n + 1), n = producers per iteration; producer rows = the loop rows whose instruction is one of the producers, reader row = the row behind the last producer; per execution = per-iteration value / the replay's issue count at that pc.

decision: As version 3, word for word: Per device. All of K1-K5 pass: M1-M4 stay installed on that device. A criterion fails because the engine does not do what the rule text says: the implementation is corrected, the build and the replay are repeated, and the addenda say so. A criterion fails although the engine does what the rule says: the rule it judges is taken out on that device by removing its leaf fields (K1 or K2: M1 and M2 together with M3, the earlier leaves restored; K3: warp_inflight_group; K4: the CS2R.CLOCK / VOTE leaves restored), the rest is judged again, and the failure is written down with its numbers. K5 (i) or (iii) failing with K1-K4 passing: nothing stays installed on that device until the cause is read from the per-cell table and written down. Criteria are not changed after the first replay.
hypotheses_full_gpu: Stated before the run, not criteria: the hardware's mio_throttle that the replay lacks (H100 loop -2.4 points of residency in full-bb2b) is partly taken up by mio_inflight; short_scoreboard (loop -1.3 / -2.3) rises where runs of LDS / S2R / LDC feed a reader; math_pipe_throttle (+2.7 / +1.8) changes little in either direction (S2R and S2UR leave the units, CS2R.CLOCK takes 2 instead of 6). Cycles may move either way and are not a criterion.
not_installed_here: A bound on S2R, LDS or SHFL in flight (appears at 16 warps and, for LDS / SHFL, from 16 per warp; depth not identified); the 2 to 7 extra cycles on the S2UR reader from 12 per run; a per-SM rate for SHFL.IDX / .UP / .DOWN; the constant paths' re-read latency at one warp (data (c)); LDCU at several warps; the same-kind / other-kind alternative of the SM pipeline; CS2R.GLOBALTIMER, CS2R.ZERO, VOTEU, R2UR.
not_allowed: No value from another machine or from the literature; no full-GPU case used to choose a rule or a value; no cell dropped after its replay is seen.

addenda.text: Against full-bb2b (68702860): H100 attribution / site / per-pc error 0.3622 / 0.2671 / 0.7828 (0.3642 / 0.2673 / 0.7842), MAPE 10.67 % (10.74), P90 21.3 %, median sim / hardware 0.911, 250 cases faster and 241 slower; B300 0.3540 / 0.3037 / 1.0573 (0.3547 / 0.3035 / 1.0573), MAPE 9.76 % (9.80), P90 17.8 %, median 0.917, 204 faster and 270 slower. Nothing moves beyond the third digit. Against the hypotheses: NOT confirmed. The new wait at issue is 0.01 % (H100) and 0.00 % (B300) of the replay's residency, and the hardware's mio_throttle that the replay lacks is unchanged (H100 loop -2.35 -> -2.40 points, B300 -0.80 -> -0.81); short_scoreboard moves by 0.07 at most (H100 loop -1.34 -> -1.27, outside -1.73 -> -1.66; B300 loop -2.27 -> -2.24); math_pipe_throttle is unchanged (+2.67 -> +2.66, +1.84 -> +1.85). The classes this protocol changes carry about 1.5 % of the replay's residency in these kernels (readers of LDS 0.27 / 0.29 %, S2UR 0.26 / 0.25 %, SHFL.BFLY 0.23 / 0.06 %, resident LDC 0.22 / 0.09 %, SHFL.IDX 0.16 / 0.13 %, S2R 0.15 / 0.12 %), and runs long enough to reach the group of four or to saturate an SM server hardly occur. The mio_throttle of the full-GPU kernels therefore comes from instructions outside this protocol (not identified here; the memory and TMA steps have to look at which pcs carry it).
